mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained unemployment above 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic output, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-on-month, combined with a flat unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tightening labor market where wage pressures may rise, increasing input costs and compressing margins, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND UNRATE monthly change ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes of strong payroll growth with flat unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% month-on-month for three consecutive months, despite stable industrial production (INDPRO), signals weakness in consumer demand that is not offset by business investment, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO monthly change within ±0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such disinflationary-tight policy episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 10% YoY for four consecutive months signals a construction-led demand expansion, which boosts materials and homebuilding equities and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY change > 10% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained strong housing starts growth.
